original.target_description: Study 1 reports separate treatment effects on correct recall and within-group recall errors. The supplied description, "Relationship between correct recall and within-group errors," does not identify which of those outcome tests is intended, or establish a directly reported relationship between the two outcomes.

es.location: Accepted manuscript pp. 9–11, Results and Figure 1 caption; supplied p. 5 locator differs from manuscript pagination.
es.quote:
The number of statements that were correctly attributed to individuals was reduced in

the treatment condition relative to the control condition in both Study 1, b = -0.93, p < .001, ... within-group recall errors was not significantly modulated by signs of infection—Study 1: b =

0.13, p = .28, 95% CI = [-0.11, 0.37]; ... unstandardized coefficients for the predicted effect of the experimental treatment (presence vs.

absence of manifest signs of infection in in-group members) on the number of correct responses,

between-group errors, and within-group errors.

notes: Identity verified internally: the coversheet identifies Michael Bang Petersen (2017), the exact supplied title, Psychological Science 28(12), 1857–1863, and DOI 10.1177/0956797617728270; document type is accepted manuscript (post-print), stated content-identical to the published article. The canonical text contains the full report, methods, results, discussion, and references. No PDF was assigned. Only original es_value_o is assigned. Target ambiguity prevents selecting a coefficient: Study 1 correct-recall treatment effect is printed b = -0.93, p < .001, 95% CI = [-1.25, -0.58] (manuscript p. 9); Study 1 within-group-error treatment effect is printed b = 0.13, p = .28, 95% CI = [-0.11, 0.37] (p. 11). Figure 1 caption (p. 10) explicitly identifies these as separate unstandardized treatment coefficients. Neither coefficient is identified as a regression of within-group errors on correct recall. No selection was made using row order or numeric matching. Candidates are retained only for parent review; target_match remains null and confidence false. Unassigned n, p, replication, and success fields are null placeholders.
